title: Kenyan Chicken Pilau
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN062 is the full chicken pilau recipe. KEN009 (Kenyan Chicken Pilau) in the original collection covers the same dish — this entry serves users browsing the chicken category. See KEN009 for additional heritage and regional detail.

desc: Pilau ya Kuku — fragrant basmati rice cooked with tender chicken pieces, deeply caramelised onions, and the classic Kenyan pilau spice blend of cardamom, cinnamon, cumin, cloves, and pepper. Quicker than goat or beef pilau but equally aromatic and celebratory.
longDesc: Chicken pilau has become the most accessible version of Kenya's beloved pilau — it cooks faster than beef or goat, making it practical for weekday celebrations and last-minute gatherings. The deeply caramelised onion base and whole pilau spices give it the same aromatic character as the meat versions, but with a lighter, more delicate result.
steps: Heat oil. Fry onions for 15—20 minutes until deeply golden brown.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Add chicken pieces. Brown for 5 minutes.
Add 2 cups stock. Cover and simmer for 25—30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Add rinsed rice and remaining 2 cups stock. Stir once.
Bring to a boil, reduce to lowest heat. Cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes.
Rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff and garnish with coriander.
chefTips: Deep caramelisation of onions is the foundation — 15—20 minutes minimum.
Chicken cooks faster than beef or goat — do not overcook during the initial simmering stage.
Remove the chicken pieces and debone before serving if preferred — makes it easier to eat.
commonMistakes: Overcooking chicken before adding rice — it becomes dry in the finished dish.

faqs.a: Yes — boneless thighs work well and make the pilau easier to eat. Add them directly without browning and reduce the initial simmering time to 15 minutes.

cookingScience: Bone-in chicken releases gelatin from the bones during simmering, enriching the stock that then cooks the rice. This gives chicken pilau a slightly richer, more complex base than boneless preparations.
sustainabilityTips: Save any leftover pilau — it reheats beautifully and makes excellent fried rice the next day.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Freeze for up to 2 months.
reheating: Sprinkle with water and reheat gently in a pot or microwave covered.
healthBenefits: One-pot meal with a balanced macro profile.
culturalNote: Chicken pilau is the most practical everyday version of Kenya's beloved celebration rice — delivering the same aromatic magic as goat or beef pilau but in a fraction of the time.
regionalVariations: Dry chicken pilau — less liquid, grainier result.
